review:
First of all, I somehow got thrown onto Hiroyuki’s route out of nowhere — it honestly felt like one of those forced-love-route plot twists 😭 I was originally aiming for Hanzo from the start, and after finishing the happy ending, I can confidently say I’d still choose Hanzo all over again. He’s such a massive kuudere/closeted softie, completely the opposite of Hiroyuki. [SPOILERS ALERT!!]

But he’s genuinely such an amazing character. His role feels almost paternal at times, while also being a mentor and companion to the heroine. On the surface, he seems cold and ruthless, as if emotions are unnecessary baggage to him. He’s called the strongest ninja for a reason: he strictly follows every ninja principle, prioritizes missions above all else, and his overwhelming strength combined with emotional detachment makes him unmatched in his field.

And then he meets the heroine — the daughter of someone important from his past.

At first, he only takes her in because of his lord’s orders to protect her. He constantly complains that she’s troublesome, speaks bluntly without caring about hurting a young girl’s feelings… but the way he calls her “musume” 😭 he really starts acting like her father for real. Scolding her, cooking for her, training her, drying her clothes and warming her up 😭😭 He honestly feels even more like her actual parent than Kando does.

BUT!!! You two absolutely deserve to fall in love and live happily together 😭 Please get married and have children immediately!!!

Hanzo’s strength is honestly heartbreaking. This route felt like a healing/redemption story for him, and it made me so emotional and happy 🥹 He’s definitely my bias in this game.

And the romance was SO sweet. Who would’ve thought that the strongest ninja, a man who values missions above everything else, would eventually break orders for her… and even choose to get injured rather than kill someone 😭😭

“I want you to live. You are the first person in this world who has ever made me feel this way.”

That ending where they retire from the ninja world and quietly live together as a happy couple was everything to me. Please let these two enjoy their peaceful married life forever 🥹

Nightshade is an otome visual novel that blends romance, political intrigue, and historical drama into a beautifully produced narrative about loyalty, betrayal, and the twilight years of the shinobi. Developed by Red Entertainment and LANTERN ROOMS and published by D3PUBLISHER, it places you in the role of Enju Ueno, the sheltered heiress of the Kōga clan during a fragile era of peace in post-Sengoku Japan. Although the clans of Kōga and Iga have nominally united under the Tokugawa regime, tensions remain just beneath the surface, and Enju’s coming-of-age mission quickly unravels into a deadly conspiracy that exposes the fault lines of this uneasy alliance. The premise is strong and immediately immersive, presenting a world where political agendas, ancient grudges, and personal desires intersect in ways that force the protagonist—and the player—to confront the harsh realities of shinobi life.

One of Nightshade’s greatest strengths lies in its audiovisual presentation. The character art by Teita is striking, filled with expressive eyes, detailed historical costumes, and beautifully rendered backgrounds that evoke forests, moonlit rooftops, and blood-stained battlefields. This painterly aesthetic, paired with a somber but elegant soundtrack, sets the tone perfectly for a story that balances romance with tragedy. The fully voiced cast, performed by veteran Japanese voice actors, elevates emotional scenes considerably. Even quieter, introspective moments benefit from the production quality, allowing players to feel present in the lives of each character. The game’s atmosphere is one of constant tension—a world where beauty and danger coexist, where every soft moment has the shadow of death behind it.

Structurally, Nightshade follows the traditional otome format: a shared common route followed by character-specific branching paths that dive deeper into the lives, motives, and emotional struggles of the chosen love interest. Each of the five main routes offers a different perspective on the unfolding conspiracy, revealing new secrets and character dynamics as you progress. These routes range in tone from tender and protective to morally conflicted and tragic, creating a wide emotional palette. Some routes emphasize political intrigue, others lean toward personal healing or forbidden affection. The writing excels most when exploring the complexities of shinobi loyalty—how duty, love, and survival often clash, and how characters navigate those conflicts with varying degrees of grace or desperation.

Although the narrative is engaging, its structure introduces some drawbacks, particularly during replays. The common route is lengthy and largely identical across playthroughs, meaning players seeking all endings will revisit the same scenes multiple times before reaching new story content. While this is a common trait in otome games, the repetition feels more pronounced here due to the story’s linear construction. Additionally, while Enju begins as a promising heroine with emotional depth, there are points—especially in certain routes—where she loses agency and becomes more reactive than proactive. This can be at odds with her training as a kunoichi and may disappoint players who prefer protagonists with more assertive or strategic roles in shaping their destinies.

Despite these issues, the character routes themselves are richly developed and offer a strong emotional payoff. Each love interest has clearly defined motivations, personal conflicts, and a meaningful relationship arc with Enju. Their stories grapple with themes such as loyalty to clan, personal sacrifice, and the vulnerable desire for connection in a world that discourages it. Some endings are bittersweet or painful, further emphasizing the dangerous environment these characters inhabit. Nightshade’s willingness to explore darker themes—betrayal, death, trauma—sets it apart from lighter otome titles and gives its romantic arcs a weight that resonates long after the credits roll.

Nightshade’s gameplay mechanics are minimal, as expected of the visual novel genre, but they support the experience well. Choice points guide the narrative down branching paths, and wrong decisions can lead to premature bad endings, encouraging players to read carefully and consider the political consequences of every action. The user interface is polished, comfortable to navigate, and includes quality-of-life features such as skip options and a flowchart for managing saves and replays. These practical touches make the game approachable for newcomers while still appealing to long-time otome fans.

In its entirety, Nightshade is a polished and emotionally rich otome visual novel that stands out for its strong production values, atmospheric worldbuilding, and mature narrative themes. It falters in its route repetition and occasional loss of protagonist agency, but its strengths—beautiful art, excellent voice acting, compelling romantic routes, and a dramatic historical setting—far outweigh these flaws. For fans of romance steeped in political tension, for players drawn to samurai-era drama, or for anyone seeking a visually striking story with emotional depth, Nightshade remains one of the genre’s most memorable titles.

Просто расскажу преимущества и недостатки.
Преимущества:
+ Очень детализированная игра. Пока что нигде такого не видела - моргание персонажей, падение лепестков на фоне, отрисовка даже второстепенных персонажей. У каждого героя свой набор эмоций и поз.
+ Интересная история. Обычно надоедает после двух рутов, а здесь начало надоедать только к пятому. И то только середина (так как она плюс минус общая у всех рутов по своей сути). А вот ближе к концу совсем все различается. Руты совершенно разные.
+ Руты на вкус и цвет: смертоносный путь, путь пацифиста, инцест, созависимые отношения, сталкер. 
+ Все герои красиво нарисованны, CG тоже очень красивые и их много.
+ Не так много воды. В каких-то моментах размышления героини слишком длинные, но, в целом, все говорят только по существу. Из-за этого и было так интересно читать. Описаний здесь минимум.
+ Интересный сеттинг с реальными историческими лицами.

Недостатки:
- Не анимированные CG. Небольшой недостаток, так как в большинстве новелл они тоже неанимированны. Но здесь эти CG не всегда совпадают с описанием, они очень короткие и большинство без динамики (когда три варианта одного CG, но на них меняется выражение лица или немного поза).
- Баги! Много мелких некритичных багов, которые снижают комфорт игры. Например: при начале новой главы, если выйти в историю (колёсиком вверх), то игра крашится и вылетает. Приходится начинать с последнего сохранения. Иногда у меня были баги в анимациях, иногда при появлении румянца у персонажа голова пропадала на секунду. 
- Самый раздражающий минус - это тупая гг. Слишком наивная. В руте Ханзо она действительно вырастает как личность за счёт убийств. В остальных рутах, особенно в руте Геккамару и Чоджиро, она просто беззащитная тряпка, которую нужно всем спасать. Она всю жизнь тренировалась, но прячется за спинами других, наблюдая как все умирают. Это было бы логично, если бы она была обычной девушкой, а не шиноби, посвятившая свою жизнь тренировкам. И читать пять раз об этом нытье надоедает очень. 
- Наитупейшие плохие концовки. Вот серьезно, нигде таких не видела ещё. Исключение - плохая концовка Куроюки: там незаметно было, что началась плохая концовка, и она интересно сделана. А вот в остальных случаях ты чувствуешь, что что-то не так, и так быть не должно. Ты не набрал сердечек и героиня решила [spoiler] захуярить пацана вместо спасения [/spoiler], серьезно??? Какой смысл??? Особенно когда знаешь, что в другой концовке она выбрала другой путь. С плохой концовки Чоджиро я вообще смеялась в голос, настолько это тупо.
Итог: визуально качественная интересная слегка затянутая новелла (59 часов на все что есть в игре). Минусы многих отомэ игр здесь присутствуют (тупая гг).

This novel is so so good, I do wonder for how long it's gonna remain my favorite otome..? Probably, and hopefully forever, that one of the major factors for getting it was the artstyle and theme.

The store page does contain pretty much all you need to know before you decided to dive-in into the bittersweet adventure full of all kinds of emotions, as well as some mystery that's to be discovered during the first and possibly second playthrough.
As per usual, as in that most novels are scripted like that, this novel does follow a main story with dialogue choices affecting your love interests, determining your ending aswell.

The characters have so rich personalities and are so unique that it's a rarity to come across.
At times, I didn't know what to do..

So many of the reactions of the characters, namely of the protagonist, have felt so relatable, it was almost as if I was reading myself rather than what has she felt, and that made me love her personality even more. And it wasn't just hers..
Many of the characters do feature their unique traits that are so standing out, their actions following them and it does make sense for why'd they do what they have done.
The predictability of the characters, yet remaining the mystery until discovered was one of the points that made me wanna keep reading and discover what's going to happen. The necessity of me having to sleep instead of reading more was almost unbearable, it was difficult to tear myself away from the screen whenever I got myself into reading this otome masterpiece.
I've wanted to know more about them. Their personalities are so interesting, I've felt completely drawn-in that the rest of the world stopped existing for me.

The story does involve some really intense situations, and because I've managed to empathize with the protagonist so much due to having some of the traits and parts of personality in common, that the novel was one if the biggest emotional rollercoasters I have ever experienced when it comes to reading.
I have lost count of how many times have I cried, felt happy, affraid, or even confused. No other novel has managed to awake such a wild side within me yet, besides about one or two exceptions.

Naturally, or rather as one would expect..
Its soundtrack has played straight into the cards of it all. It was all pitch perfect.
Each track, each situation tied to it.. It was matching. Nothing was off, and the music has only intensified everything that's been reflected there back to me.
When the protagonist got sad, I got sad.
When the protagonist felt embarrassed, I have felt embarrassed.
...
This sort of [i]connection[/i] has made it so special. Each track have had its place, and I thoroughly enjoyed every little bit of vibration that got back to me.
There were tracks that have made me alerted, somewhat scared yet determined to find out what's going on and how is it going to end, just like there were tracks that have made me so happy I could burst, as well as sad that I wanted to comfort not just myself, but the portrayed characters in my own fairytale reality that I imagined on top of it all.

If anyone's looking for an otome genred novel, do know that this is gonna be and too likely even remain one of the bests if not the best you can ever come across.
There's no point hiding it, as the novel's got so much to offer in terms of the play with one's emotions that getting immersed becomes so easy, capturing one's attention within such a short while that it will feel truly unique and special.
- Before I finish this review here.. I shall add that certain portions of text aren't properly translated, but that's less than say, twenty lines across the whole novel. In other words, those encounters will be met once in a blue moon.

This review..
I'm not even sure if it's gonna be of any help to you between deciding whether to get the novel or not, seein' that it's become a pretty much yet another.. Eh, confusing mysterious detective [i]essay[/i] of its own, but I can't help it.
Expressing myself without the proper words, unfortunately also affected by the small vocabulary of mine, couldn't have felt any better.

So, please do enjoy yourself reading through this otome masterpiece if you decide to go for it, and hang in there..
Some forces that are to make you all emotional are to be felt while reading this, and I have no doubt you're gonna love it.
Have fun!

I love this game!! 🥹

- The voice acting is GREAT, not only the love interest ones, but all the characters too! To be honest, I bought this game just because I saw that Kenjiro Tsuda was voicing one of the LIs, heh.
- The art is GORGEOUS; I couldn't help but screenshot every CG I saw even though all of them were in the gallery after seeing them once.
- The soundtrack is good, but to me it wasn't memorable apart from the good ending song (絶えざる花 / MAKOTO), which I listened to way too much...

Nightshade's story basically branches to two slightly different storylines ("a" and "b"), so my route order recommendation to avoid major spoilers is:
a) GOEMON > HANZO > KUROYUKI
b) CHOJIRO > GEKKAMARU

And lastly, my thoughts about the routes without spoiling it too much: 

[b]Hanzo's route: [/b] Slow burn and healthy relationship! What I like the most here is how both of them learn and grow with each other, all that made love flourish in their journey, making them better individuals. Enju's character development here was really good; this is the only route she fought and stood her ground; in the other routes she was just there to be protected by the LI. The way they fell in love with each other felt so natural, I loved it so much :>

[b]Goemon's route: [/b] Super fun, cute and wholesome! Goemon is too sweet, I felt warm and fuzzy inside and couldn't stop smiling at his good ending. I wasn't expecting much cuz flirty LI love interests aren't my first choice, but Goemon's actions made the romance in this route feel really mundane, I enjoyed it very much! 

[b]Gekkamaru's route: [/b] Filled with angst and devotion. I felt so emotional throughout the whole route [strike] (I cried a lot) [/strike] and by the ending, I just couldn't feel much, I was numb even to the good ending, which was bittersweet because of everything that happened. Everything was just so unfair.

[b]Kuroyuki's route: [/b] Yandere. I'm not into characters with this type of personality, but his background for explaining why he became obsessed with Enju is just tragic and well written, that made me sympathize with Kuroyuki. The route is very enjoyable and heartbreaking, it has a great finishing to one of the branching storylines. I especially liked his Bad Ending just because my heart was destroyed when I realized what was happening :')

[b]Chojiro's route: [/b] I don't know what to talk about this route, I do understand the struggles Chojiro went through, but I didn't sympathize with Chojiro at all, the story felt bland to me and I basically played through with my mind blank. I don't really know if this route didn't really add anything to the plot (apart from a bit of info on the other characters) or if it was because this was my last route. But yeah, this is the only route I didn't like playing.

[i] [b] Nightshade [/b] — это визуальная новелла в жанре отомэ, переносящая игрока в Японию конца эпохи Сэнгоку. Главная героиня, Эндзю, является дочерью главы клана ниндзя Кога и с детства обучалась искусству куноичи. Вместе со своими друзьями она отправляется на свою первую миссию, после которой оказывается втянута в таинственный заговор. [/i]

Несмотря на то, что я редко играю в отомэ-игры, [b] Nightshade [/b] сразу привлекла мое внимание своим выразительным визуальным оформлением, антуражем древней Японии и сеттингом 
(๑•̀ㅂ•́)و✧.


[b] Плюсы: [/b]

• [b] Атмосфера и сюжет [/b]
 История с первых минут погружает в эпоху Сэнгоку, умело сочетая романтику с интригами и драмой. Каждая линия раскрывает сюжет по-новому и вызывает сильные эмоции.
• [b] Визуальная составляющая [/b]
 Арты потрясающие, визуальный стиль игры безупречно передает дух времени и делает каждую сцену запоминающейся. (´︶`)♡
• [b] Музыкальное сопровождение и звук [/b]
Один из самых впечатляющих саундтреков среди визуальных новелл и игр в целом. Плюс ко всему очень атмосферные и качественные звуковые эффекты (дождь, ветер, птицы и т.д.).
• [b] Романтика [/b]
Романтика развивается в меру, естественно и плавно, что делает ее более ценной.
• [b] Лучший мальчик — [spoiler] Ханзо Хаттори!  [/spoiler] (⁄ ⁄•⁄ω⁄•⁄ ⁄)  [/b]
Его концовка оставляет ощущение умиротворения, а голос сейю — просто шедевр. ✧(>o<)ﾉ✧


[b] Минусы: [/b]

• [b] Развитие главной героини [/b]
В некоторых рутах ее личностный рост ощущается слабо. В одних историях она меняется и становится сильнее, а в других остается почти такой же ( ･ั﹏･ั).
• [b] Сходная структура сюжета [/b]
Независимо от выбора персонажа, основной ход событий остается неизменным. Было бы интереснее, если бы разные маршруты делали акцент на разных аспектах истории. Например, [spoiler]  в ветке Ханзо Хаттори можно было бы глубже раскрыть сюжет вокруг покушения на его господина Токугава Иэясу. [/spoiler]
• [b] Проблемы с разрешением [/b]
Из-за того, что игра была разработана с фиксированным разрешением, на моем 2K мониторе в оконном режиме изображение слишком маленькое, а в полноэкранном разрешение не соответствует. Кроме того, в полноэкранном режиме иногда ломается звук в некоторых эндингах.

She has her moments of being a hard worker and sucking it up, but for the most part she's weak, in the way and winy. I dislike MC like this. 3. The choices don't really matter much. Either you pick the right one or you don't. Not much else to it. This is a minor con for me though, as I feel like most otome are like this.

4. A little uncomfy: (Trigger warning) [spoiler] Kuroyuki's route is a bit intense and really sad. I didn't dislike it. I like when games have dark/sad themes. But dude was just creepy imo. By far my least favorite route. Also, lots of age differences that could be potentially grooming? Idk I tried not to think about the older cousin thing too much with Chojiro lol. Or the fact that Hanzo is probably twice MC's age. Tbh Gekkamaru was the least problematic. So if you're sensitive to anything like that, just be aware. I still think the game was a lot of fun and this wasn't a big enough issue for me to not recommend the game. [/spoiler]


Pros:

1. Artwork is beautiful

2. Voice acting is impeccable. By far the best I've experienced playing an otome. Hanzo alone had me swooning fr

3. Writing: Each route is similar but different enough to make it worth playing them all imo. I also liked that this was pretty tame. Nothing spicy. I like a slow burn with low spice and that is also hard to find sometimes.

4. UI / options: The skip and quick save/load features are so good. A lot of these games don't implement them well or usefully so you still end up having to re-read stuff you don't want to and wasting a lot of time. After I finished the good endings for all the routes, I was able to plow through to the bad endings within an hour using these features. 

Overall I highly recommend the game if you like otome. I think Hanzo and Gekkamaru have the best routes, so if you only want to play a couple, I recommend those.

First of all! You right click the upper portion of the screen to access the menu on PC. That took me forever to figure out, and I freaked out thinking I couldn't save. That's also the menu where you can see your relationship points with the 5 romanceable guys or change the settings to make skipping faster/slower, etc.
This visual novel is a fantastic blend of squee-worthy romance and political intrigue. The first 3-4 chapters follow the same story line, allowing you to make choices and gain romance points with your desired character.  Then there are a few minor changes depending on who you have the most romance points with and a mission split (Gekkamaru and Chojiro follow one mission while Kuroyuki, Hanzo, and Goemon follow the other mission). Around chapter 5, whoever you have the most romance points with (if there is a tie between two or more, the game will choose the highest one to the left) becomes your locked in romance story from then on with unique pacing and plot. 
It really felt like a different story for each play through - I was very impressed. Usually with multiple romance options, you pretty much just play the same game over and over to get the achievements, but this was really fun to read each character's story. Each had similar major plot points as anchors, but there was a lot of fluidity in the story details between those plot points. 
If you want a dramatic, cry-your-eyes-out, never-saw-that-twist-coming type first play through - pick Chojiro first. If you want a twist and some crying but in a slightly less dramatic and intense fashion, try Gekkamaru first. If you're into dark and broody bad-boy with a tragic backstory trope, Kuroyuki is your boy. If you prefer to play the innocent shy girl falling for a playboy with an earnest heart and a carefree attitude, go with Goemon. If you're the type who likes to feel in control of a situation or if you don't like to be confused trying to puzzle out the intrigue and just want things laid out for you, Hanzo's got your back. 
My recommended play order would be Chojiro --> Kuroyuki --> Hanzo --> Gekkamaru --> Goemon ...... Hanzo was my favorite. Chojiro was a close second favorite, though.

To start off, I never really had the intention to buy this game but everyone kept praising it so I bought it last year. I only found the time to play it recently(after my finals were done) and I immediately went on to try it. It took me 6 days in total to finish with 33 hours of gameplay. Minor-ish spoilers will be included(can't guarantee that's all but I'll try my best)

I did Goemon->Hanzo->Chojiro->Gekkamaru->Kuroyuki for the route order and before I started any actual route, the order of which LI I liked so far was Hanzo>Goemon>Chojiro>Gekkamaru=Kuroyuki.

Here's my quick thoughts on each of the routes/characters:

1. Goemon

-Ngl, I was looking forward to his route because I like flirty characters :). His route started off great, got me catching feelings for him(as expected). I have nothing much to say other than I was kind of disappointed in the later half of his route. It wasn't bad, it's just that I feel like the ending was too rushed. You'll find that I'll have similar opinions on the others' routes as well. Route is a 6.5/10 for me.

I feel like I'd grown like him more on the other routes lol he's just so.. gentlemanly. I find myself disappointed when he just leaves abruptly like he normally does. I love how he's just there to help because he slightly likes her in all of the routes lol.

2. Hanzo

-I HAD NO EXPECTATIONS FOR HIM. He isn't my type to begin with(he's too old for my liking) but DAMN. His route was amazing, had me feeling giddy all the time. I loved loved LOVED Enju in his route, she is such a badass there in contrast to her normal damsel character in everyone else's route. Like Goemon's, his ending was also slightly rushed but I didn't mind it that much here because it blended in well anyways. 7.5/10 --Actually, make that an 8/10 lol simply bc he's a great character and once you finish the game you'll find that you love him more than you did during his route lol.

I kind regret doing him second because in the last three routes, I just continued on falling for him even more💀. How can he be so.. lovable?? Anyways, that's it, I just love him.

3. Chojiro

-I really liked him at first, he was stoic, but not cold. Plus, he's very pretty. His route made me cry a lot and I would've liked it more if I didn't hate the Koga gang as much. I found them to be very hypocritical especially in his route and they had a fair amount of screentime as well, I was just irritated most of the time. Also, I found the pacing to be horrendous. Too many things were happening at once, which in a case, is actually what makes his route so overwhelming but at the same time underwhelming because you don't linger on a certain problem for long. I didn't like the ending as well, not because it was bad, I feel like it could've been better, the whole route could've been better. 5/10.

As a character? Meh. He doesn't amaze me. He and Hanzo have the same mindset but Hanzo is just better in every way lol I'm sorry.

4. Gekkamaru

-I was very hyped for his route and boy it did not disappoint. I found it to be the most romantic out of the five and the CGs were just absolutely beautiful. The pacing was great except for, yeah, the ending. I felt likethey didn't give us enough time to digest all of the information in the ending and just threw all of the ♥♥♥♥ right at us. Nonetheless, I liked it, the romance makes up for it. 9/10

I love him sm in every route even though he can be a bit overbearing. How can you get mad at such loyalty and sincerity? He's just perfect. Perfect route to end the game with.

5. Kuroyuki

-I saved him for last because I liked him the most out of the cast(I like brats). While I did expect how his route was gonna go, I was not prepared for how yandere he is. Anyway, I feel like his route was the best paced of them all. Nothing felt overly rushed(considering how short each route actually is) and I feel like I was given proper time to digest my thoughts about him. Unexpectedly, his route did not impact me the most though(which I thought would, which is why I chose him last), doesn't mean it was bad, it was great. I didn't really connect with him as a character but I do sympathize with his situation. I think it's just a me problem though. His route could've been perfect except for the fact that THERE WAS 0 KISS CGS?! HOW TF DOES HE HAVE THE MOST KISS "SCENES" WITH ENJU BUT HAS 0 CGS OF IT. It was still pretty romantic though despite that. 9/10 best boy.

He's a character you'd want to hate but physically cannot if you've played his route lol. Also, these lines from his route tho

"I wanted to make a world for us, but you love the world you're in."

"If I can't live with her in this world, then I'll make this world right for her"

I wish we'd gotten more brother moments but that's a dream too good to be true. In the end, the order of characters I liked ended up being Chojiro>>Goemon>Hanzo>=Kuroyuki>=Gekkamaru(I'm indecisive). The game could've been miles better(not that it was bad ofc) if the routes were longer and more fleshed out, you find that it's just lacking in extra details which makes it hard to properly connect with the game.

Overall, the game was entertaining. I wouldn't say it's a masterpiece nor but since I play on pc and got it while on sale, it's more than worth compared to what I paid. I wished this was longer but it's past midnight and I want to pass out of drowsiness. okay so i'll try not to include any or only a minimal spoilers below:

I'll go in order of the routes i played.

Kuroyuki: I loved his route the best. It was also my first, and they always had good moments together. His sad backstory always made me never look at him the same in other routes. I bought this game mainly because of him. He's the yandere. 10/10

Chojiro: I was concerned to do his route since i thought their dynamics were too similar to siblings, but omg i cried so much. i felt as though his is the most realistic or at least pessimistic route. Their dynamics were adorable too, since he kind of spoils her. i was really drawn to how reliable he was. Enjoyed his route alot!

Gokemon(?): Super subpar. although extremely wholesome, i felt literally no sparks, no romance! i felt like his rote was the most idealistic and happy, but after doing it after such a heavy route, honestly it felt hollow. So unfortunately I couldn't enjoy his route. it was meh.

Gekkamaru: Another route i was worried about. He seemed the most vanilla and although i was right, i was pleasantly surprised by their dynamic. i actually liked it, even though i usually don't like it when the female takes the lead sometimes. It worked well here. They were quite cute. Again something tragic occurs, but after already crying in chojiro's i wasn't as emotional. It didn't hit as hard. But still quite nice. Not in love, but nice.

Hanzo: so gotta preface this by saying my irl personality would not be compatible with this guy at all. i hated, absolutely hated their initial dynamic. all he has to save him is his pretty face. CONCLUSION: order of routes matter. depending on how you are i would recommend Goemon(?) first, then do the guy you're most interested in between gekkamaru and chojiro, then hanzo last.
